mainText: Good morning. Here is your curated AI briefing for Tuesday, November 10, 2026. Anthropic is moving toward its initial public offering with significant details emerging regarding its leadership’s financial stake. According to the company's recent S-1 filing, its seven co-founders—Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, and Christopher Olah—each plan to sell 3,378,378 shares. With an initial price range of 70 to 78 dollars per share, each founder stands to cash out approximately 250 million dollars at the mid-range price of 74 dollars. Despite these sales, the founders will retain collective voting control through supervoting Class F shares, holding 51.1 percent of the total vote. This structure ensures the founding team maintains strategic direction even as their equity stake in Class A shares reduces to a combined 22 percent. The IPO is highly anticipated, with board members Reed Hastings and Christopher Liddell already signaling interest in purchasing shares. The founders, who left OpenAI in 2021 due to disagreements over AI development, will continue to emphasize their commitment to AI safety, a foundational principle of the company. In the infrastructure sector, Google DeepMind has launched Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier model. Designed for complex, multi-step tasks such as software engineering, cybersecurity, and scientific research, Carbon is positioned as a more intensive companion to the previously released Gemini 4 Argon model. DeepMind states that Carbon excels at deep reasoning and extended verification loops, making it suitable for tasks that require exhaustive exploration. The company is also introducing a feature called /swarm, which enables users to coordinate teams of autonomous agents, allowing for real-time tracking of complex workflows. Carbon is currently available to paying developers, enterprises, and Google AI Ultra subscribers, matching the pricing of the Argon model. This release aims to provide high-performance reasoning for professional and scientific applications where precision is paramount. Also in infrastructure, NVIDIA is expanding its contributions to open-source software, specifically targeting the management and security of AI agents. At the KubeCon conference, the company announced the donation of OpenShell to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation. OpenShell is a runtime environment designed to provide deterministic security controls for autonomous agents, allowing organizations to govern how agents access tools and data. This is a critical development for enterprise adoption, as it provides a standardized way to enforce safety policies across different deployment environments. Additionally, NVIDIA is contributing to the Google-led Agent Substrate project, which facilitates the scaling of agent workloads on Kubernetes. By integrating these tools, organizations can manage agent lifecycles, preserve environments between tasks, and optimize compute resources, effectively building a more secure and efficient foundation for enterprise-level AI factories. In the business sector, Oura is acquiring AI-native primary care startup Counsel Health for 625 million dollars. This acquisition follows Oura's recent postponement of its own IPO, signaling a strategic pivot to broaden its service offerings. Counsel Health, which integrates medical AI with access to licensed physicians, has been operating within the Oura app since June. The acquisition aims to leverage Counsel’s AI capabilities alongside Oura’s existing physiological data to provide users with a more comprehensive suite of preventative and chronic care services. Counsel CEO Muthu Alagappan will join Oura as chief clinical AI officer, bringing his team of 70 employees to the company to facilitate this expansion. In other developments, Hugging Face has announced that organizations can now link their accounts to Google Cloud, allowing usage fees to be processed through existing Google Cloud billing rather than individual credit cards. This change is designed to simplify procurement and integrate AI tool costs into established corporate cloud budgets. Separately, OpenAI is launching free, hands-on ChatGPT workshops for caregivers in five U.S. cities to help build practical AI skills, demonstrating a commitment to expanding AI literacy.
